name: AisleWise
one_liner: A browser-native 3D digital twin of a picking floor fed by one real month of UCI Online Retail II orders, where every picker route is an exact dynamic-programming tour on the aisle graph, a simulated-annealing slotter is the opponent the player must beat, and every number on screen is a deterministic held-out replay, not a claim.
why_it_wins: From an optimisation lens, 4.2 is the only problem statement where the must-have visual and the algorithmic core are the same object: the route drawn on the floor IS the objective function. That lets us put a genuinely serious OR stack on stage without a backend: (1) the Storage Location Assignment Problem (SLAP, NP-hard, QAP-like) solved by simulated annealing with O(affected-orders) incremental delta evaluation, (2) an inner exact routing DP (Held-Karp over the aisle-graph shortest-path metric) so the outer metaheuristic's objective is itself exact, (3) the classical cube-per-order-index baseline (Heskett 1963) the brief demands, (4) Hall (1993) S-shape routing as the "what humans do" ablation, and (5) a temporal held-out split (first half of the month to optimise, second half to score) that exposes SA's in-sample overfit honestly. Judges remember three images: the path drawing itself along the aisles while the metres tick, a ghost picker losing a race to the player's layout on the same real invoice, and the warehouse visibly re-slotting itself while the convergence curve falls. Why not 4.3 (the deepest OR story on paper): it needs a Python solver backend, and tonight's verified free-tier facts are hostile (HF Gradio/Docker Spaces now need PRO; Render free spins down after 15 min with ~60 s cold start and 0.1 CPU), its map is synthetic coordinates on a fake city, and every BKS gap becomes a Q&A liability; its in-browser ALNS variant is deep but 2D and less legible in 5 minutes. 4.2 is fully static (Vercel/Cloudflare Pages), deterministic, key-free, offline after first load, under-picked by ML-student teams who fear three.js, and parallel agents can add measured stretch goals (batching, heatmap, congestion) on top of the same simulate() function. Every scout independently ranked it first on feasibility, visual ceiling and judge reward; the technical-depth scout ranked it second only to 4.3, and the depth gap closes once exact routing + SA + ablations are in.
demo_script:
0:00-0:25 HOOK (slide 2, then switch to live URL): "Pickers walk more than they pick. Where a product sits decides the walk. This is a 3D twin of a forward-pick area fed by November 2011 of UCI Online Retail II: N invoices, M pick lines, top-120 SKUs, coverage X% (numbers read off the app's Data panel, not the slide)." Camera opens on a slow 3/4 isometric swoop (drei CameraControls setLookAt, 2 s) over 6 aisles of instanced racks, boxes coloured by pick frequency.
0:25-1:05 M1+M2 DATA-DRIVEN TWIN: Operator clicks a box: side card shows StockCode 85123A, "WHITE HANGING HEART T-LIGHT HOLDER", picks this month, orders containing it. Press REPLAY: header shows "Invoice 5814xx, 6 lines, 16 Nov 2011 09:12"; the picker leaves the dock, the cyan path DRAWS ITSELF ahead of him along the aisle centre lines (never through a rack), the metres and seconds counters tick with motion animate(); a small badge: "animating 1 of 1,8xx held-out orders, totals from headless replay in a Web Worker". WOW #1.
1:05-1:35 EXACT ROUTING TOGGLE: Operator flips the routing switch S-shape -> Exact (Held-Karp). Same order, path re-draws, counter drops (e.g. 71 m -> 58 m). Caption: "per-order optimal tour by DP over the aisle-graph distance matrix; S-shape is what a human picker does". Judges who know OR lean forward here.
1:35-2:35 M3 GAME + REPLAY RACE: Operator drags the T-light holder from aisle 5 to the bay next to the dock (drei DragControls with snap; click-slot-A-then-slot-B fallback), swaps two more fast movers. Press SCORE: KPI tiles animate: Original 41.9 km / Baseline COI 30.2 km / You 32.7 km on the held-out second half (illustrative; real values from eval). Press RACE: a 35%-opacity ghost picker re-walks the same invoice on the original layout while the solid picker walks the player's layout; both counters run and diverge live; floor tiles under both accumulate heat. WOW #2.
2:35-3:35 THE OPPONENT: Press ANNEAL (seed 42 shown, 8 s budget). Convergence chart (ECharts) draws live from the COI value downward; accepted swaps fly as boxes lerping between bays; iteration counter runs (~10-15k swaps). It stops at SA = 27.x km. Table shows opt-set vs held-out side by side with the sentence "held-out gain is smaller than in-sample gain, as expected" printed from the numbers. Load the 60 s/5-seed precomputed SA layout: "SA(60 s) mean +/- sd". WOW #3.
3:35-4:15 EVIDENCE PANEL: one screen: data meta (removed C-invoices, non-product codes, duplicates), split sizes, Original/COI/SA/Player x opt/test, routing ablation (S-shape vs NN+2-opt vs exact), SA vs plain descent vs random-restart at equal budget, 200 random layouts distribution with the three layouts marked. Toggle BATCHING (cart of 4 orders): km/order falls again, measured by the same simulate().
4:15-4:45 LIMITATIONS, spoken while the heatmap of rack visits is on screen: forward-pick area only (top-120 SKUs, coverage stated), the "original" layout is a declared StockCode-order convention because the dataset has no layout, single level, constant 8 s pick time and 1.2 m/s walking, one picker in headline numbers, 2011 UK gift retailer with wholesale customers.
4:45-5:00 CLOSE: QR codes for live URL and repo; "every number you saw is reproduced by `npm run eval` at commit <hash>".
Q&A cards (20 s each): split rule; why StockCode order as original; coverage; Held-Karp cutoff (n<=10, count of fallback orders); how delta evaluation is verified (unit test: delta == full recompute); why SA beats COI (order affinity); what breaks it (multi-level, congestion); who wrote which file.
wow_visual: Scene (React Three Fiber 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 on three 0.186.1, Vite 8.3.5, React 19.3.1): (a) Racks: one InstancedMesh of 120 bay frames (box geometry, slate MeshStandardMaterial) + one InstancedMesh of 120 SKU boxes with per-instance colour via instanceColor (viridis-like ramp from pick frequency; switchable to visit-heat after a replay); 3 draw calls for the whole warehouse; floor is one plane with a GridHelper-style shader-free texture; dock is an amber slab with an Html label. No shadows, no post-processing by default; a Quality toggle enables @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1 Bloom (luminanceThreshold 0.9, mipmapBlur) + SMAA for strong laptops; devicePixelRatio capped at 1.5; frameloop "always" but the scene is tiny, so 60 fps on integrated GPUs. (b) Picker: procedural low-poly (capsule body + cart box + two cylinder wheels) so no asset pipeline; optional Kenney CC0 glTF swap if time remains. Movement: the Web Worker returns the full grid polyline for the animated order; useFrame advances a parametric position at 1.2 m/s x speed multiplier (1x/4x/20x), with an 8 s pick pause rendered as a bob animation and a slot flash. (c) Self-drawing path: drei <Line> (Line2) with points = polyline.slice(0, k) where k grows ahead of the picker, lineWidth 3, cyan, plus a dashed grey "ghost" Line for the before-layout route; the two never intersect racks because they come from the grid Dijkstra. (d) Counters: motion 14.5.0 animate(from, to, {onUpdate}) for metres/seconds; KPI tiles with layout animations when values change. (e) Camera choreography: drei <CameraControls> (camera-controls 3.1.2) presets Overview / Dock / Follow (setLookAt(..., true) with smoothTime 0.6), Follow lerps target to the picker. (f) Replay Race: two picker instances, the ghost at opacity 0.35 (transparent material, depthWrite false), both driven from the same order on different layouts; floor heat tiles = one InstancedMesh of 0.5 m cells whose instanceColor accumulates per visit. (g) Anneal animation: the worker posts accepted swaps every 250 iterations; the scene lerps the two boxes' instance matrices across bays over 300 ms (small in-flight list), while an ECharts 6.1.0 line chart (animationDurationUpdate 200) draws the convergence curve of current J and best J, with the COI value as a markLine. (h) Interaction: raycast click on box instance (instanceId) opens the SKU card; drag via drei <DragControls> constrained to the floor plane with snap-to-nearest-empty-or-swap on release; click-A-then-B swap as the robust fallback; undo stack. (i) UI shell: Tailwind 4.3.3 dark theme, left KPI column, bottom timeline/controls, right evidence drawer; lucide-react icons; projector-legible 18-24 px numerals. (j) Evidence page: ECharts bar (layouts x sets), scatter/violin of 200 random layouts with markers, ablation table.
wow_technical:
Four layers, all pure TypeScript in web/src/sim (no framework), shared verbatim by the Web Worker, the scene, and eval/run.ts (Node via tsx) so README numbers and on-screen numbers come from identical code.
1) Aisle-graph metric. layout.json: aisles=6, baysPerSide=10 (2 sides) -> 120 slots, slotPitch 1.2 m, rackDepth 1.0 m, walkway 2.0 m (aisle pitch 4.0 m), front/back cross-aisles 3.0 m, optional middle cross-aisle flag, dock at the front-left corner (classic P&D point), grid cell 0.5 m. Walkable cells = aisle centre lines + cross-aisles; each slot has an access node on its aisle centre line; BFS/Dijkstra (4-neighbour, 0.5 m edges) from each of 121 nodes over ~1,700 cells -> Float32Array D[121x121] + predecessor maps for polylines. Walking distance therefore follows aisles by construction; the drawn path is the shortest path on the grid.
2) Exact per-order routing. routeCost(stops): Held-Karp bitmask DP over {dock} U stops for n<=10 (10^2*2^10 ~ 100k ops), tour = dock -> all stops -> dock (metric satisfies triangle inequality); for n>10 nearest-neighbour + 2-opt + Or-opt until no improvement (same function used everywhere; count of such orders reported, expected <2%). Ablations: S-shape (Hall 1993: traverse every aisle containing a pick end-to-end, return on the last) and NN+2-opt. Tests (vitest 3): Held-Karp == brute-force permutations for n<=7 on 500 random orders; S-shape >= exact on every order; D symmetric and triangle-inequality-clean.
3) Slotting = SLAP (order-oriented, cf. Mantel, Schuur & Heragu 2007; Frazelle & Sharp 1989). Baseline (required): COI/ABC: SKUs ranked by pick lines desc assigned to slots ranked by D[dock][slot] asc (Heskett 1963, unit cube). Opponent: simulated annealing over the SKU->slot permutation, move = swap two SKUs; delta via an inverted index SKU->orders so only orders containing i or j are re-routed (cached per-order costs; typed arrays; ~70 orders per swap on average); T0 = median|delta| of 200 sampled swaps / ln 2 (so the median uphill move is accepted with p=0.5), geometric cooling to T0/1000 over the wall-clock budget (8 s live, 60 s in eval), best-so-far tracked, seeded mulberry32 PRNG with the seed displayed; frequency-weighted proposal of i (fast movers proposed more often) as an optional accelerator. Correctness test: in debug mode every accepted delta is asserted equal to a full recompute (the test an OR judge asks for). Ablation rows at equal budget: plain descent (T=0), random-restart descent, SA; 5 seeds mean +/- sd. Objective J(L) = sum over opt-set orders of routeCost; evaluated separately on the held-out set. Context row: 200 uniformly random permutations -> distribution of km with Original/COI/SA percentile.
4) Measurement. Temporal split: invoices dated 1-15 Nov 2011 = optimisation set, 16-30 Nov = held-out test set (slotting is decided on the past and pays off in the future). Metrics: total walking km, mean metres/order, mean seconds/order (distance/1.2 m/s + 8 s per line), for Original (StockCode-order convention), COI, SA, Player, on both sets; routing-policy ablation on both the original and SA layouts; batching (stretch) km/order for cart capacity 1..4 via seed-earliest + min-insertion-cost savings on the union of stops. Why non-trivial: a bilevel structure (outer metaheuristic whose inner objective is an exact DP), incremental evaluation that makes 10-15k exact re-routings per second feasible in a browser worker, an honest in-sample vs out-of-sample report, and classical baselines an expert recognises by name. What proves it: the eval tables plus the live anneal whose curve the judge can watch from the COI value downward with a seed they can change.
mvp_mapping:
M1 (pre-processing -> JSON): prep/prep.py (Python 3.12, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0, run with python -I) reads the 7.16 MB Online Retail II parquet, filters InvoiceDate in 2011-11, drops Invoice starting with "C", rows with Quantity<=0 or Price<=0, StockCodes not matching ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ (removes POST, D, M, S, DOT, BANK CHARGES, CRUK, AMAZONFEE, ADJUST, gift_*), exact duplicate rows (counted), aggregates to one pick line per (Invoice, StockCode), ranks SKUs by number of pick lines (visits, not quantity) and keeps the top 120, emits web/public/data/orders_2011-11.json with meta {rows_in_month, cancelled_removed, nonproduct_removed, nonpositive_removed, duplicates_removed, lines_total, lines_covered, coverage_pct, orders_opt, orders_test, lines_per_order {median,p90,max}}, skus [{i, code, desc, picks, orders}], orders [{id, t, set:"opt"|"test", lines:[sku idx]}]. The app's Data panel displays meta verbatim; clicking any box shows its code/description/picks from this JSON.
M2 (3D grid warehouse replaying orders with aisle-following walking and live counters): web/src/scene renders racks, aisles, dock and one animated picker; replay takes an order from the JSON, the worker returns the exact route and grid polyline, the picker walks only along aisle/cross-aisle cells, the path is drawn on the floor, and the metres/seconds counters are driven by the same distance and time model used for scoring; the invoice ID and line count are displayed during replay; a "replay whole month" button scores all orders headlessly in <200 ms and shows the totals.
M3 (game mode with before/after and automatic baseline): drag or click-swap SKUs between slots; SCORE re-runs simulate() on exactly the same order list for Original, COI baseline (fast movers nearest the dock, computed automatically from pick frequency and D[dock][slot]) and the Player layout, on the opt set and the held-out set; before/after km, metres/order and seconds/order shown in a table with deltas; the SA opponent is an additional automatic layout the player can try to beat; the Replay Race animates ghost vs player on the same invoice.
stretch_goals: Batch picking (brief stretch): cart capacity k=2..4, seed = earliest order, add orders by minimum insertion cost of their stops (savings), route the union with routeCost; km/order curve vs k on the held-out set; toggle in UI
Heatmap of rack visits (brief stretch): per-slot visit counts from the headless replay mapped to instanceColor; aisle-level bars; near-free once instancing exists
Leaderboard of player layouts (brief stretch): localStorage + export/import layout JSON (no backend, no keys); shows km on the held-out set and the seed

Several pickers with congestion (brief stretch): time-stepped simulation of 2 pickers on consecutive orders; when both occupy the same aisle segment the later one waits 2 s per blocked step; reports added seconds and % orders delayed; reported separately from headline numbers
SA(60 s) x 5 seeds precomputed layout shipped as data/sa_best.json with mean +/- sd in README; live 8 s anneal shows the mechanism
Optional middle cross-aisle layout variant (multi-block) to show the grid metric generalises; same code path
Order-affinity view: co-pick matrix of top SKUs (ECharts heatmap) explaining why SA beats COI
Explain-my-route panel: lists the exact tour order and S-shape order side by side for the replayed invoice
data_plan: Dataset: Online Retail II, UCI Machine Learning Repository id 502, licence CC BY 4.0; cite Chen, D. (2019). Online Retail II [Dataset]. UCI ML Repository, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D. Obtain (verified tonight from campus): curl -L -o data/raw/online_retail_II.parquet "https://huggingface.co/datasets/vancevo/online-retail-ii/resolve/main/data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet" (7.16 MB, 1,067,371 rows = UCI's published count, columns Invoice, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, Price, Customer_ID, Country). Fallback: Kaggle anonymous zip curl -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" "https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/mashlyn/online-retail-ii-uci" (15.2 MB -> online_retail_II.csv 94.85 MB). Do not use the UCI zip directly (truncates from campus; fetch_ucirepo(id=502) returns data_url null). Record the mirror choice and the row-count check in DEV_LOG. Keep raw data out of git (.gitignore data/raw); commit the download script and the <1 MB derived JSON. Month: November 2011 (peak volume; most orders and lines). Preprocessing (prep/prep.py, Python 3.12, pandas 3.0.6 + pyarrow 26.0.0, run as python -I prep/prep.py --month 2011-11 --top 120 --split-day 16): filter month; drop C-invoices; drop Quantity<=0, Price<=0; keep StockCode ~ ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$; drop exact duplicate rows (count); collapse to one pick line per (Invoice, StockCode) because a pick visits a slot once regardless of quantity (stated); rank SKUs by pick-line count; top 120; orders = invoices with >=1 covered line (also report count with >=2); temporal split by invoice timestamp (<16 Nov = opt, >=16 Nov = test). Expected magnitudes (to be replaced by computed values printed in meta): ~3,000 invoices in the month, coverage of the top-120 SKUs ~20-30% of lines, median 3-5 covered lines per order, <2% of orders with >10 covered stops. Held-out evaluation: all layouts optimised (COI, SA, player) only see the opt set; headline numbers are reported on the test set with the opt-set numbers alongside. Assumptions declared in README and in-app: walking speed 1.2 m/s, 8 s per pick line, dock at front-left, layout dimensions, original layout = top-120 SKUs sorted by StockCode filled aisle-major (the dataset contains no layout). Attribution in README (Data section), in the app footer, and in the pitch.
architecture: Components: (1) prep/prep.py (offline, Python) -> web/public/data/orders_2011-11.json (+ data/sa_best.json produced by eval). (2) web/src/sim (pure TS, zero deps): layout.ts (grid, Dijkstra all-pairs D + predecessor maps), route.ts (heldKarp, nnTwoOpt, sShape, routeCost), replay.ts (simulate(layout, orders, policy) -> totals + per-order costs + optional polylines), slotting.ts (coiBaseline, anneal with incremental delta + inverted index, descent, randomRestart), batching.ts (stretch), rng.ts (mulberry32). (3) web/src/worker/sim.worker.ts: message protocol {score, anneal, route, batch}; posts progress every 250 SA iterations (J, best, accepted swaps) and final results; keeps the main thread at 60 fps. (4) web/src/scene (R3F): Warehouse.tsx (InstancedMesh racks/boxes/heat tiles), Picker.tsx, PathLine.tsx, CameraRig.tsx, Interactions.tsx (raycast click, DragControls, swap). (5) web/src/ui: KpiPanel, Controls (replay/score/anneal/race/routing toggle/quality), SkuCard, EvidenceDrawer (ECharts), DataPanel (meta). (6) web/src/store.ts (zustand 5): layouts {original, coi, sa, player}, selected order, results, undo stack. (7) eval/run.ts (tsx in Node, imports the same sim modules) -> eval/results.md + eval/results.json with commit hash, date, seeds; `npm run eval` is the single reproduction command. Data flow: JSON fetched once at load -> store -> worker (scores, anneal) -> store -> scene/UI; no network calls after load; no API keys; .env.example contains only a comment that no secrets are required. Compute location: 100% browser (main thread rendering + one Web Worker for optimisation/scoring); Python only offline for preprocessing; Node only for the eval script. Deployment target: Vite static build (dist/) on Vercel Hobby (vercel.json SPA rewrite), backup Cloudflare Pages/Netlify (all files <25 MiB; JSON <1 MB; three + R3F + drei + echarts ~900 KB gzipped); site works offline after first load; local `npm run preview` on two laptops as venue fallback plus the recorded MP4.
stack: @react-three/drei@10.7.9 (CameraControls via camera-controls@3.1.2, Line, Html, DragControls, Instances)
vitest@3.x (Held-Karp vs brute force, delta == full recompute, S-shape >= exact)
Vercel Hobby static hosting (backup: Cloudflare Pages / Netlify)
build_plan: Repo: public GitHub from 22:00 IST tonight; first commit = README skeleton, .env.example (comment only), DEV_LOG.md, LICENSE (MIT), .gitignore (data/raw, node_modules, dist, .env), prep/download.sh. Agents work on branches feat/sim, feat/opt, feat/scene, feat/ui; one human merges to main at least hourly (reminder every 45 min) with conventional messages; `eval:` commits land before any `tune:` commit. Agent A - Data + simulation core (4 h, 22:00-02:00): prep.py and JSON schema (1 h); layout.ts grid + Dijkstra + polylines (1 h); route.ts Held-Karp/NN+2-opt/S-shape with vitest brute-force tests (1.5 h); replay.ts simulate() + worker protocol skeleton (0.5 h). Agent B - Optimiser + evaluation (4.5 h, 23:00-03:30, starts from A's interfaces agreed at 22:30): coiBaseline, inverted index, SA with incremental delta + assertion test (2 h); descent/random-restart/seed loops (0.5 h); batching.ts (1 h, stretch); eval/run.ts producing results.md/json + sa_best.json with 60 s x 5 seeds (1 h). Agent C - 3D scene (6 h, 22:30-04:30): Vite+R3F scaffold with instanced racks/boxes/floor/dock and camera presets (1.5 h); picker + path drawing + counters wired to worker (1.5 h); click SKU card, click-swap, DragControls with snap, undo (1.5 h); ghost Replay Race, anneal swap animation, heat tiles, quality toggle, DPR cap (1.5 h). Agent D - UI/UX, deploy, docs scaffolding (5 h, 22:30-03:30): app shell, KPI tiles, controls, evidence drawer with ECharts, data panel (2.5 h); Vercel deploy of walking skeleton by 23:45 (floor + one replayed order + counters) for progress reviews (0.5 h); README sections, Mermaid architecture diagram, DEV_LOG template, eval table auto-inclusion (1 h); laptop perf pass and projector-legibility pass (1 h). Integration/QA (3 h, 04:30-07:30, one agent + one awake human): wire all panels to the worker, determinism check (two SCORE clicks identical), eval vs app number cross-check, 4-year-old-laptop test in Chrome and Edge, bug fixes, demo-path hardening (preloaded demo invoice, preset camera, 8 s anneal). 07:30-10:30 stretch goals in priority order: heatmap, batching toggle, leaderboard, congestion (only if green). 10:30-11:00 feature freeze tag; 11:00-12:30 final `npm run eval`, README/DEV_LOG numbers from results.md with commit hash, limitations; 12:30-13:30 OBS demo recording (<=5 min) and 3-min YouTube cut; humans build the .pptx (10 slides, python-pptx) in parallel; 13:30-14:15 LinkedIn + X posts (#NEXAI2026, repo + live URL, 20 s clip); 14:15-14:45 smoke test on a different laptop and phone, final deploy; 14:45 submit. Human ownership for Q&A: Human 1 owns sim/ (layout, route), Human 2 owns slotting.ts + eval, Human 3 owns scene/, Human 4 owns ui/ + prep.py + docs; each reads and annotates their module before 12:00.
risks: Laptop/projector performance stutters -> 3 draw calls via InstancedMesh, no shadows, no post-processing by default (Quality toggle), devicePixelRatio capped at 1.5, worker for all compute, tested on an older laptop before 14:00, hidden FPS readout

SA inner loop too slow in JS (Held-Karp per affected order) -> incremental delta with inverted index and cached per-order costs, typed arrays, n<=10 DP cutoff, wall-clock budget with iteration counter shown, 60 s precomputed layout shipped as data so the live anneal is theatre of a mechanism not the source of headline numbers
Delta evaluation bug makes SA results wrong -> debug assertion delta == full recompute on every accepted move in tests; eval re-scores every final layout from scratch with simulate()

Top-120 coverage of order lines looks low -> state coverage % prominently, frame as the forward-pick area, parametric --top so judges can see 200 if asked; orders with no covered lines are excluded and counted
3D drag-and-drop fiddly on a trackpad -> click-A-then-B swap is the primary path in the demo script, drag is an enhancement, undo stack
Held-Karp blow-up on big orders -> hard cutoff n<=10 with NN+2-opt+Or-opt fallback used consistently in search and scoring, count reported
Vercel build or deploy failure -> identical static dist/ deployed to Cloudflare Pages as backup URL in README, local `npm run preview` on two laptops, recorded MP4
Judges ask where is the AI -> the metaheuristic optimiser is the AI opponent; the slide names SLAP, Held-Karp, SA, COI, Hall; no LLM is a deliberate zero-key, zero-cold-start choice stated in DEV_LOG
Commit cadence slips overnight -> agents commit on branches at least hourly, a human (rotating sleep) merges to main hourly, DEV_LOG timestamps every merge
Data mirror doubt -> row count 1,067,371 and column set verified against UCI's published description; Kaggle fallback script committed; attribution to UCI id 502 CC BY 4.0 everywhere
Determinism challenge (replay twice) -> no randomness in scoring; SA seed displayed and settable; identical numbers on repeated SCORE verified in QA
honesty_plan: Single source of truth: `npm run eval` (eval/run.ts importing the same sim modules the app uses) writes eval/results.md and results.json with commit hash, date, seeds and budgets; README tables are pasted from results.md only, and the app's Evidence drawer recomputes the same quantities live from the same JSON, so judges can compare screen vs README. Held-out discipline: temporal split (1-15 Nov optimise, 16-30 Nov test) fixed in prep.py and tagged `eval-frozen` before any tuning; COI, SA and player layouts see only the opt set; headline numbers are test-set numbers with opt-set numbers beside them and the in-sample vs out-of-sample gap stated in a sentence. Baselines and ablations reported, not just the win: Original vs COI vs SA vs Player; S-shape vs NN+2-opt vs exact; SA vs descent vs random-restart at equal budget; 5 seeds mean +/- sd; 200 random layouts distribution for context. Declared conventions in README, in-app footer and pitch: the dataset has no warehouse layout, so the Original layout is StockCode order (a stated convention); walking speed 1.2 m/s and 8 s per pick line are assumptions; dock at front-left; one picker, single level, no congestion or cart capacity in headline numbers (congestion/batching reported separately as stretch); picks counted as visits (one per order-line) not quantities; orders with >10 covered stops use heuristic routing (count given); coverage % of order lines by the top-120 SKUs given in meta. Watch-outs handled and shown: C-invoices removed (count), non-product codes removed by regex (list and count), duplicates removed (count), aisle-following distances by construction (path drawn on the floor from the grid shortest path), simple geometry for laptops. Limitations section: 2011 UK gift wholesaler data, forward-pick area only, no ergonomics/levels, no replenishment, slot sizes equal, results depend on the declared parameters (a sensitivity row for pick time 5/8/12 s is included). Provenance: UCI id 502 CC BY 4.0 citation with DOI, mirror used and why (UCI truncation from campus) logged in DEV_LOG; no personal data; no LLM, no keys; .env.example states no secrets required; AI coding tools (Claude Code) declared in README with the human review process per module; DEV_LOG records decisions (why 4.2 over 4.3, why SA over GA/tabu, why Held-Karp over Ratliff-Rosenthal), experiments table, and rejected approaches.
